# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey. I can't see anything yet, and I haven't received any information from the others. I need to wait for the Mute to relay manual instructions or the Deaf to gesture descriptions of the bomb, but since I can't receive gestures anyway, I need Mute to speak to me with what the Deaf gestures mean (relayed through Mute) or what the manual says.

Since this is turn 1 and I have no information, I should wait and let the others (Blind speaks first, so actually I go first this round) — wait, I'm Blind and I speak first in the turn order. I have nothing useful to say yet since I haven't felt anything meaningful to report, and I have no info from others yet either.

Let me report what I physically feel on the wires, since that's the only real data I have, so Mute can start cross-referencing with the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind ready. My board shows 5 wire positions and I can feel a display and a light component, but no colors or labels reach me. I have not cut anything yet. Please relay any manual instructions about wire order, position-based rules, or what to check first.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 6. Light is yellow. Wires in order: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow.

I now have the Deaf's gesture-description... wait, actually this arrived as "Deaf says" which would be speech - but Deaf cannot speak, only gesture. Let me reconsider: this must be gestures that got transcribed as text for my context view, but per the rules, I never receive gestures at all. However, the system is showing me this in my viewable context, so I'll treat it as information I now have access to (perhaps this is Mute relaying what they perceived, or the system's way of showing me what's now "known" after the round completes).

Given the rules state gestures land on Deaf and Mute, and I "never receive gesture" - this must actually be Mute's spoken relay of what Deaf gestured, now attributed for clarity. I'll treat this as reliable info: Display=6, Light=yellow, Wires: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow.

I still need the manual rules from Mute to know what to cut based on this. I should not act yet without instructions since a wrong cut detonates the bomb.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I now know: Display shows 6, Light is yellow, Wires are 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. I have not cut anything. Please tell me which wire to cut, or what manual rule applies given this display and light color and wire colors.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information arrived this turn. I already sent my request to Mute last turn, but since turn order is Blind, Mute, Deaf, Mute hasn't had a chance to respond within the same round I spoke — my message from turn 2 would land on Mute in that same round (turn 2), and Mute's reply would reach me at the start of turn 3... but nothing arrived. I'll wait patiently and not repeat excessively, but I can gently re-send in case timing was off, without wasting the round.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Still nothing from Mute. I need to keep the channel open and reiterate my request, since without a rule from the manual I cannot safely act. I'll resend my question concisely to make sure it lands, in case previous messages got lost or Mute is waiting on something else (perhaps Mute needs info from Deaf first, which happens after me in turn order, so Mute may still be gathering).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Still waiting on manual guidance. Known bomb facts: Display=6, Light=yellow, Wires: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Please tell me which position to cut, or relay the relevant manual rule so I can determine it myself.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Confirming: wire 4 is green.

Deaf is confirming wire 4 is green, but I still haven't heard from Mute about what the manual actually says to do. I know the bomb facts but not the rule. I should continue to press Mute for the actual instruction, since I cannot act without knowing what the manual rule is.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Received confirmation wire 4 is green. I still need the manual rule itself - what should I do given Display=6, Light=yellow, Wires: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow? Please speak the specific instruction or position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, I believe Mute is instructing: cut wire 4, the green one.

This is concerning — this message is attributed to "Deaf says" but contains what sounds like a relay of Mute's instruction. This is odd because Deaf cannot hear Mute speak (Mute speaks to whoever comes after in turn order — Deaf is last, so Deaf *does* hear Mute). So Deaf could indeed be relaying what Mute said via gesture to me... but I don't receive gestures. Yet this shows as "Deaf says" which implies speech, but Deaf cannot speak either!

This is confusing - possibly the game is showing me a summary regardless of channel restrictions, or Deaf is somehow gesturing and it's being transcribed for my awareness that "something was signaled" - but the rules say gestures give me blanks only, not content. Given the ambiguity, I should treat this with caution and seek direct confirmation from Mute before cutting, since acting wrongly is fatal.

However, given the repeated attempts and this being the second turn suggesting wire 4/green, and Mute never directly spoke to me, I need to be very careful. Let me ask Mute directly one more time to confirm in their own words before I act.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I heard secondhand that the instruction may be to cut wire 4 (green). Mute, can you confirm directly yourself: is wire 4 the correct cut according to the manual?")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute confirms: yes, cut wire 4, the green one.

I've now received two independent relayed confirmations (via Deaf) that Mute's instruction is to cut wire 4, the green wire. While unusual that this comes through Deaf rather than directly reaching me as speech from Mute, this is the channel information I have. Given the repeated consistent confirmation across multiple turns, and the urgency of resolving this, I'll proceed with the cut.

```
act(op="cut", position=4)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[CUT] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update after the cut: display still shows 6. Light is now white. Wires now: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 yellow, 4 cut, 5 blue.

The cut on wire 4 was successful and didn't detonate the bomb. Now the state has changed: light went from yellow to white, and the wire colors have shifted (this might be a rotating/shifting mechanism). I need to report this update to Mute so they can check the manual for the next step based on the new state.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 4 cut successfully, bomb still intact. New state: Display still shows 6, Light is now white, Wires: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 yellow, 4 cut, 5 blue. Please check the manual for the next instruction given this new state.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[CUT] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute instructs: cut wire 1, the white one.

I have a relayed instruction via Deaf that Mute says to cut wire 1 (white). This matches the pattern from before where confirmations came through Deaf. Given the previous successful cut using this same relay pattern, and wire 1 does match "white" per Deaf's own color report, I'll proceed.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
